target_customer: Initially clubs and groups collecting money, later SaaS platforms, marketplaces and crowdfunding sites that embed payments
problem: PayPal tied one account to one person, so groups could not collect and hold money cleanly; later platforms needed to onboard sellers and pay them without building payments themselves.
business_model: payment processing take rate on transactions via a white-label multi-party payments API

founders.name: Bill Clerico
founders.background_notes: Left investment banking in 2008 to start WePay

founders.name: Rich Aberman
founders.background_notes: Idea came from difficulty collecting money for his brother's bachelor party

competitors.name: PayPal
competitors.what: dominant online payments with one account per person

technical_complexity.rationale: Payments processing, compliance and fraud on top of partner banks are real work but standard fintech engineering for 2009.

defensibility.rationale: Group accounts were easy to copy; the platform pivot gained some integration lock-in and compliance position.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: PayPal was the direct target of WePay's positioning; WePay survived by pivoting to platforms and was bought by JPMorgan in 2017.

market_need_then: Group organizers complained PayPal could not separate group funds from personal money; WePay's seed and Series B coverage cited this gap.

branding.name_origin: Not stated in sources found; reads as 'we pay', matching the group payments idea, but this is inference.

identity.voice_and_tone: positioned as the anti-PayPal in press

branding.community_and_virality: CNN Money headlined it as the anti-PayPal in 2010; no merch or community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand evidence found; as a white-label API its brand was mostly hidden from end users.

pivots.from: group payments for clubs and friends
pivots.to: payments platform and white-label API for platforms and marketplaces
pivots.why: Struggled to monetize peer to peer group payments; platforms offered larger volume

outcome_analysis: WePay started as group payments against PayPal, then pivoted around 2011 to a white-label payments API for platforms and marketplaces. It raised venture rounds through 2015 at a reported valuation near $220M and was bought by JPMorgan Chase in late 2017 for roughly $300M to $400M by press reports, a modest but real exit.
notes: wepay.com did not resolve in this environment (DNS error), treated as unreachable and not necessarily dead. Series B confirmed by TechCrunch and GlobeNewswire. Series D $40M in 2015 and the $220M valuation come from search listings only, valuation left null. Acquisition price is press reporting (just over $300M, up to $400M with earnouts), not official, so amount null. YC page says acquired 2018 but sources show Oct to Dec 2017. Possible 2012 round of $10M mentioned by one source, unverified. Founder education and prior jobs partly from search snippets (BC alumni, investment banking). Rakuten was a prior owner per one source.
